sentences.text: This animal stands as the biggest known hadrosauroid, reaching lengths between 15 and 17 meters and weighing 13 to 16 metric tons.
It featured a beak without teeth, yet its jaws held roughly 1,500 small teeth designed for grinding food.
Scientists believe a significant opening near the nose might have been sealed by flexible skin used to create vocalizations.
In 2016, Gregory S. Paul proposed reducing the size estimates to 15 meters and 13 metric tons, though it still holds the title of largest hadrosaur.
Researchers first named the species in 1973 based on over five partial skeletons dug up between 1964 and 1968.
Its massive legs supported a bulky frame as it moved as a heavy quadruped.
Although it usually walked on four legs, the animal could also stand upright on its hind legs because its hands ended in hooves.
It gathered tough vegetation with its beak and crushed the plants into a paste using its many small cheek teeth.
Specimens once thought to be Zhuchengosaurus maximus in 2007 were later reclassified as Shantungosaurus, with variations explained by different growth stages.
These creatures roamed Asia roughly 77 to 70 million years ago during the Campanian and Maastrichtian periods.
